cards.explanation: The answer is brother. The message opens, "This is what your brother Israel says…" (Numbers 20:14). Moses reaches out family to family, and I think that's a smart way to knock on a door. It's like showing up with a fresh batch of cookies and saying, "It's me, your kin!" Hard to slam the door on that.

The answer is False. The message says, "The Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers…" (Numbers 20:15). Kindly doesn't show up anywhere in that sentence. Moses tells it plainly so the king knows what Israel has walked through.

The answer is an angel. The message says that when they cried out, the LORD "…heard our voice, sent an angel, and brought us out of Egypt." (Numbers 20:16). They cried, and He heard. That's the whole story in one breath.

The answer is permission to pass through. The message says, "Please let us pass through your land." (Numbers 20:17). Israel isn't asking to move in. They just want to get through, and they say please.

The answer is True! Israel says, "We will not go through any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well." (Numbers 20:17). Fields, vineyards, wells. They list it all, one by one, like a baker promising not to touch ONE crumb on the cooling rack. I'd have caved on the spot, friends. I can't even promise that about my own dough.

The answer is the King's Highway. Israel says, "We will stay on the King’s Highway; we will not turn to the right or to the left until we have passed through your territory." (Numbers 20:17). Straight through, no side trips. That's a promise you can picture.

The answer is no, or they'll come out with the sword. Edom answers, "You may not travel through our land, or we will come out and confront you with the sword." (Numbers 20:18). Israel asked so nicely, and the answer is no with a sword attached. That one stings.

The answer is pay, friends. Israel says, "…if we or our herds drink your water, we will pay for it." (Numbers 20:19). They're not asking for a handout, they're pulling out the wallet! Water for a whole herd, and they're offering to cover the bill. That's the kind of customer every shop owner prays for. I once got a quarter's worth of respect in my life, so I know what it's like when somebody offers to pay.

The answer is True! Israel says, "There will be no problem; only let us pass through on foot." (Numbers 20:19). Hear that "only"? That's the whole ask. No fields, no vineyards, just feet on the road. I've seen bakers ask for more than that when they want one extra cookie, and I still said yes.

The answer is that they come out with a large army. Edom "…came out to confront the Israelites with a large army and a strong hand." (Numbers 20:20). Two nos, then an army. Israel asked politely twice and got a crowd of soldiers for it.

The answer is False. The passage ends, "…Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through their territory, and Israel turned away from them." (Numbers 20:21). Israel turns away. No fighting through, even with that army standing right there.
